notes: Perfect claim overlap (C103, C104, C122, C123) but fundamental disagreement. LLM finds strong evidence that AMTs undergo conformational changes during transport. Peer reviewers challenge this, arguing fluorescence changes could result from binding-induced protonation changes rather than transport-cycle conformational changes, without requiring significant conformational movement.

High overlap on transport-inactive mutations (C76, C77, C78, C79). LLM concludes this strongly demonstrates fluorescence reports transport activity. Peer reviewers acknowledge the correlation but state this evidence is insufficient to definitively distinguish binding from transport without additional discussion or data, particularly regarding the suppressor screen experiments.

Strong agreement on transferability to other transporters (C56, C89, C90, C91). Both recognize the successful development of AmTrac1;2 and MepTrac as an important technical advance and validation of the approach across multiple ammonium transporters, despite uncertainty about the exact mechanism being reported.

Strong agreement on sensor development (C7, C53, C58, C61). Both find the creation of AmTrac by cpGFP insertion convincing, with concentration-dependent fluorescence changes well-demonstrated. Reviewers describe work as 'convincing, satisfying, and carefully done.' LLM also includes C59, C60 not addressed by peer review.

Agreement on uncertainty about binding vs. transport (C54, C106). Both acknowledge the sensors cannot definitively differentiate between substrate binding and specific transport steps. However, peer review is more critical, stating authors 'repeatedly conflate' binding with transport throughout the paper, while LLM notes authors appropriately acknowledge this limitation.

Agreement on correlation with electrophysiology (C63, C64, C65). Both recognize that fluorescence responses correlate well with voltage-clamp measurements, including Km values. Peer reviewers state signal 'nicely tracks the NH4+ transport activity as measured directly by voltage-clamp methods.' LLM also addresses C8, C9, C62 not in peer review.

Limited overlap (C107). LLM expresses uncertainty about what sensors report. Peer reviewers support the authors' acknowledgment of alternative interpretations but criticize that this caveat appears only once while the rest of the text assumes transport. Different emphasis on the same underlying issue.

Agreement on technical utility (C10, C11). Both recognize the sensors as an important technical advance for monitoring transporter activity in vivo, with advantages over existing methods. LLM addresses broader claims (C100, C101, C131, C132) about applications not specifically evaluated by peer review.

Minimal overlap (C68, C72). LLM finds single-cell imaging data strongly supports that AmTrac specifically reports ammonium-dependent processes. Peer reviewers express major concern that features used to argue fluorescence requires transport 'do not seem to differentiate ammonium binding and transport.' Fundamental disagreement on interpretation.

Limited overlap (C82, C85). LLM finds suppressor screen provides strong evidence fluorescence reports transport-related conformational changes. Peer reviewers note suppressor experiments 'might' argue for transport but require more information on binding to be definitive. LLM more confident in interpretation than peer reviewers.

Minimal overlap (C67) but agreement. Both accept that single-cell imaging demonstrates concentration-dependent responses. LLM addresses broader characterization (C68-C72) while peer review focuses on correlation with electrophysiology measurements.

Minimal overlap (C8) but agreement. Both accept concentration-dependent fluorescence responses. LLM emphasizes Km correlation with transport kinetics while peer review focuses on successful sensor development.

Minimal overlap (C9). LLM finds concentration-dependent responses strongly support sensor validity. Peer reviewers uncertain whether this demonstrates transport versus binding, stating authors conflate the two concepts throughout the paper.

Minimal overlap (C100). LLM supports claim that sensors can monitor transporter activity in vivo. Peer reviewers uncertain about what exactly is being monitored (transport vs. binding), though they acknowledge technical utility.
Claims C73, C74, C75 about linker optimization and AmTrac-LS variant only addressed by LLM. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific technical details.
Claims C86, C87, C88 about AmTrac-100μ variant with altered kinetics only addressed by LLM. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this engineered variant.

Claims C126, C134, C135 about broader generalizability to other protein families only addressed by LLM. LLM appropriately notes this requires further validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation.

Claims C44, C45, C108 about transceptor concept only addressed by peer review. Reviewers acknowledge the concept but criticize inadequate explanation in the paper. No corresponding LLM evaluation found.
